title: GPU provisioning redispatch and queue compaction playbook for hosted capacity events
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a combined set of follow-ups from the Feb hosted-GPU exhaustion incident: large tenant queue buildup, cascading admission throttles, and delayed autoscaler ramp. The goal is a pragmatic, testable playbook that reduces end-to-end recovery time, prevents tenant amplification, and provides safe redispatch/provisioning behavior during noisy bursts.

Background:
During the Feb 18 incident we observed three correlated failures: (1) tenant request amplification on cold pools created long-lived queues, (2) the autoscaler’s warm-up window and hysteresis prevented timely provisioning of supplemental capacity, and (3) admission-layer throttles caused head-of-line blocking rather than evicting/redispatching individual requests to healthy pools. Previous tickets addressed tuning throttles and backoff but did not produce an integrated solution.

Scope and goals:
- Implement a queue compaction fast-path that collapses redundant in-flight prefix work for identical model+prompt fingerprints (opportunistic dedup).
- Add a redispatch policy so long-waiting requests can be moved to alternate compatible pools when capacity exists, avoiding wholesale tenant-level eviction.
- Introduce a short-duration surge provisioning mode: fast-bump capacity with conservative preemption/fallback rules to avoid permanent overcommit.
- Update runbooks, dashboards, and SLA escalation paths to reflect the above controls and measurable SLOs.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not redesign the autoscaler; it adds a short-lived surge control layer that can be rolled back independently. It also does not change cost-accounting for billing (follow-up PM work required).

Why this differs from prior work:
Existing tickets focused on admission scoring and slow autoscaler tuning. This plays on three underutilized levers: compacting redundant work, redispatching individual requests (rather than tenant-level shed), and a controlled short-term provisioning fast-path. Combined they reduce queue pressure and make recovery less binary.

Success metrics (target):
- Median queue wait for impacted requests decreases by 60% during similar load spikes.
- Recovery time-to-baseline capacity reduced from 18 minutes to <6 minutes for 90th percentile events.
- No more than one user-visible 5xx per 10k requests attributable to redispatch in canary tests.

Risks and mitigations:
- Deduplication correctness: must not merge requests with side-effecting calls or different agent contexts. Mitigation: conservative fingerprinting and explicit opt-out header.
- Redispatch-induced duplication: user may receive reordered or duplicated responses if backend semantics not idempotent. Mitigation: best-effort idempotency keys and per-tenant config flags; fall back to eviction if not safe.
- Cost/regression risk from surge provisioning: mitigate via strict caps, TTL on provisioned nodes, and export of spend telemetry for early rollback.

Work breakdown and milestones:
- Design (owner: Ravi) — 2d: API for request fingerprinting, redispatch policy semantics, and surge-provisioning guardrails. Link: https://confluence.redwood/internal/capacity/redispatch-design (draft)
- Prototype queue compaction (owner: Lina Chen) — 5d: in-memory prefix/KV coalescing in runtime; unit tests + load microbench. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582
- Canary redispatch + surge provision (owner: Ravi) — 7d: feature-flagged rollout to one region with synthetic tenant traffic harness; dashboarding and tracing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2211
- Autoscaler integration (owner: Marcus Lee) — 3d: tune autoscaler fast-path triggers; metrics plumbing for cost telemetry.
- Runbook & dashboards (owner: SRE team) — 2d: update incident playbook, add alert for surge-provisioning throttles and redispatch error rates.

Observability and tests:
- New metrics: queue_compaction_hits, redispatch_attempts, redispatch_success_rate, surge_provision_nodes, surge_provision_cost_seconds.
- Trace spans to show lifecycle: receipt -> admitted? -> compaction_hit -> redispatched? -> executed -> response.
- E2E canary scenarios simulating tenant spike with 10k rps synthetic workload and 80% long-context token churn.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge prototype behind feature flag and unit tests.
2) Small canary in us-west-2 with synthetic tenant as traffic generator (2h smoke). Monitor redispatch_success_rate and user-visible 5xx.
3) Increase to three regions with throttled rollout if metrics stable for 12h.
4) Flip feature flag for full hosted production and enable 24h watch with on-call SRE.

Longer-term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- PM work to map surge provisioning spend back to billing (PM ticket required).
- Explore model-level prewarm hints exposed by model registry (research ticket).

Notes and past references:
- Incident postmortem: ENG-11288 (Feb hosted GPU saturation)
- Prior throttle tuning: ENG-18499
- Admission scoring exploration: ENG-61234
